When models were quite limited in what they could do, ironically all you could be literally was a “wrapper” because you were effectively delivering tokens back to the user with a custom prompt or some limited RAG. 

But in a world of agents using tools, tasks that run on for hours or days, workflows that kick off agents, agent swarms that need to be coordinated against a goal, data sources that are domain specific, model routing that requires domain-specific routing, implementation that requires real change management of the workflow instead of “just type into this chat box”, it’s very very possible that specialization of these systems goes up more. 

Obviously this doesn’t apply to everything - the closer you are to the labs core use-cases the tougher this play gets, but I’d argue we’re going to see autonomous systems for a wide range of job functions that weren’t practical to build out before. We’ll see this in security, life sciences, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and many other fields. And while we’re at it use the words tape out, memory/CPU shortage too. 

Make it 50/500 on a memo 🤝", "createdAt": "2026-10-20T02:20:04.000Z", "url": "https://x.com/nikunj/status/2112368222809034980", "likes": 36, "retweets": 1, "replies": 7, "isQuote": false, "quotedTweetId": null}, {"id": "2112219327881761008", "text": "A few weeks ago, I was ranting about multiplayer AI experiences and that's when @ekuyda shared an early preview of Wabi 2.0..

Truth be told, I was one of the early users of Wabi 1.0 and while the design was gorgeous, it frankly never "stuck" with me.

But, in moments of downloading this edition, I was immediately hooked. 

It just gets the "paradigm" right imo. There are two types of personal agents today: 1) Singleplayer iMessage or Muse types - while useful it's hard to compartmentalize them when many things are going on 2) Build your own multiple chat Hermes agents - while that's useful and can share context, they live forever

Wabi has this great paradigm of orchestrator (which is the main agent) and topic specific episodic chats that are for a single purpose. You can share these individual chats with folks (for example the school one with my wife). And these are generated proactively AND don't need to stay forever (which is important).

For example, for my recent NY trip, it was generated based on a flight it saw, provided help where needed, and then after the trip was done, it was archived. Same with my 2025 taxes. 

My only critique so far it's TOO proactive, the apps can be better and they need to dial both of those in, but this is a wonderful product that everyone should try!

(I know it's shocking to see this in today's day and age, but this is neither paid, nor an investor, just a fan)", "createdAt": "2026-10-19T16:28:25.000Z", "url": "https://x.com/nikunj/status/2112219327881761008", "likes": 46, "retweets": 6, "replies": 7, "isQuote": true, "quotedTweetId": "2112212804979880239"}]}, "tweets": [{"id": "2112368222809034980", "text": "Waiting for someone to sell me a peptide factory built in a data center which is also a robotics neolab that is somehow co...

{"builder": {"source": "x", "name": "Aaron Levie", "handle": "levie", "bio": "ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI", "tweets": [{"id": "2112404676436222170", "text": "The big bitter lesson question in the applied AI layer is that as models get better and better, what is the best way to diffuse that intelligence into an enterprise. 

Ironically, I’d argue that as models are getting more capable, and can handle longer running tasks and better tool use, the ability to differentiate on a domain by domain basis goes up instead of down. 

When models were quite limited in what they could do, ironically all you could be literally was a “wrapper” because you were effectively delivering tokens back to the user with a custom prompt or some limited RAG. 

But in a world of agents using tools, tasks that run on for hours or days, workflows that kick off agents, agent swarms that need to be coordinated against a goal, data sources that are domain specific, model routing that requires domain-specific routing, implementation that requires real change management of the workflow instead of “just type into this chat box”, it’s very very possible that specialization of these systems goes up more. 

Obviously this doesn’t apply to everything - the closer you are to the labs core use-cases the tougher this play gets, but I’d argue we’re going to see autonomous systems for a wide range of job functions that weren’t practical to build out before. We’ll see this in security, life sciences, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and many other fields. {"builder": {"source": "x", "name": "Nikunj Kothari", "handle": "nikunj", "bio": "partner @fpvventures - investing in seed/A. previous: early hire @meter, @opendoor, @atlassian & others. love @shimoleejhaveri + 👦👧", "tweets": [{"id": "2112422877949751491", "text": "Tenzing on Apple TV+ is a must watch..

The acting, the direction, the music. 

I can’t believe this was all shot in real environments and with zero green screens. 

Literal goosebumps.", "createdAt": "2026-10-20T05:57:15.000Z", "url": "https://x.com/nikunj/status/2112422877949751491", "likes": 12, "retweets": 0, "replies": 1, "isQuote": false, "quotedTweetId": null}, {"id": "2112368222809034980", "text": "Waiting for someone to sell me a peptide factory built in a data center which is also a robotics neolab that is somehow collecting first party uniquely differentiated data..

And while we’re at it use the words tape out, memory/CPU shortage too. 

Make it 50/500 on a memo 🤝", "createdAt": "2026-10-20T02:20:04.000Z", "url": "https://x.com/nikunj/status/2112368222809034980", "likes": 36, "retweets": 1, "replies": 7, "isQuote": false, "quotedTweetId": null}, {"id": "2112219327881761008", "text": "A few weeks ago, I was ranting about multiplayer AI experiences and that's when @ekuyda shared an early preview of Wabi 2.0..

Truth be told, I was one of the early users of Wabi 1.0 and while the design was gorgeous, it frankly never "stuck" with me.

But, in moments of downloading this edition, I was immediately hooked. 

It just gets the "paradigm" right imo. There are two types of personal agents today: 1) Singleplayer iMessage or Muse types - while useful it's hard to compartmentalize them when many things are going on 2) Build your own multiple chat Hermes agents - while that's useful and can share context, they live forever

Wabi has this great paradigm of orchestrator (which is the main agent) and topic specific episodic chats that are for a single purpose. You can share these individual chats with folks (for example the school one with my wife). And these are generated proactively AND don't need to stay forever (which is important).

For example, for my recent NY trip, it was generated based on a flight it saw, provided help where needed, and then after the trip was done, it was archived. Same with my 2025 taxes. 

My only critique so far it's TOO proactive, the apps can be better and they need to dial both of those in, but this is a wonderful product that everyone should try!

(I know it's shocking to see this in today's day and age, but this is neither paid, nor an investor, just a fan)", "createdAt": "2026-10-19T16:28:25.000Z", "url": "https://x.com/nikunj/status/2112219327881761008", "likes": 46, "retweets": 6, "replies": 7, "isQuote": true, "quotedTweetId": "2112212804979880239"}]}, "tweets": [{"id": "2112368222809034980", "text": "Waiting for someone to sell me a peptide factory built in a data center which is also a robotics neolab that is somehow co...
